steps.title: Import React and useState from 'react'
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from the 'react' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing React and useState from 'react'
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.seedCode: // Import React and useState from 'react' here
steps.expectedOutcome: The import statement for React and useState is added to the file.
successCriteria: The code includes a valid import statement that imports both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState. This gives you access to React's core functionality and the useState hook for managing state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the import statement needs adjustment. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. You need to import both React and useState from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Create the main TodoList component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named TodoList that returns JSX. The component should be defined with TypeScript syntax and return a JSX element.
steps.hint: You can define it as a function declaration or arrow function. Make sure to specify the return type as JSX.Element.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the TodoList component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A TodoList component is created with proper TypeScript typing that returns JSX.
successCriteria: Component named TodoList is defined
Component returns JSX
Component has proper TypeScript typing (JSX.Element return type)
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the TodoList component with proper TypeScript typing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your TodoList component returns JSX and has proper TypeScript typing.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't quite right. Remember to create a functional component named TodoList that returns JSX with TypeScript typing.

steps.title: Define the Todo type interface
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface named 'Todo' with three properties: 'id' (type number), 'text' (type string), and 'completed' (type boolean). Place this interface above the TodoList component.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions inside curly braces.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Todo interface is defined with the correct property types, enabling type-safe todo items throughout the component.
successCriteria: The code includes an interface named 'Todo' with 'id: number', 'text: string', and 'completed: boolean' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the Todo interface with all required properties and correct TypeScript types.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Check that your interface has exactly three properties: 'id' (number), 'text' (string), and 'completed' (boolean).
steps.feedbackWrong: The Todo interface isn't defined correctly. Make sure to use the 'interface' keyword with the name 'Todo' and define all three properties with their TypeScript types.

steps.title: Initialize todos state with useState
steps.instruction: Inside your TodoList component, initialize a state variable named 'todos' using useState. The initial state should be an empty array of Todo objects (use the Todo interface you defined earlier).
steps.hint: Use the useState hook with a generic type parameter to specify the array type: useState<Todo[]>([]).
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of initializing an array state with useState
const [items, setItems] = useState<Item[]>([]);
steps.expectedOutcome: The todos state variable is initialized with an empty array of Todo objects, ready to store todo items.
successCriteria: State variable named 'todos'
Uses useState hook
Initial value is empty array []
Type annotation Todo[] (via generic or type inference)
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the todos state with an empty array of Todo objects. This gives us a place to store our todo items.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check: Did you name the state variable 'todos'? Is the initial value an empty array? Did you specify the Todo[] type?
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Inside the TodoList component, use useState to create a state variable named 'todos' that starts as an empty array of Todo objects.

steps.title: Initialize input state with useState
steps.instruction: Inside your TodoList component, initialize a state variable named 'inputText' using useState. Set its initial value to an empty string.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. The state variable should hold a string value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a new state variable 'inputText' initialized to an empty string, ready to store user input for new todo items.
successCriteria: The code should include a useState call that declares a state variable named 'inputText' with an initial value of an empty string. The state variable should be properly typed as a string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the inputText state variable. This will allow you to track what the user types in the input field for new todo items.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but there might be an issue with your state initialization. Make sure you're using useState with an empty string as the initial value, and that the state variable is named 'inputText'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The inputText state variable wasn't properly initialized. Remember to use the useState hook with an empty string as the initial value, and name the state variable 'inputText'.

steps.title: Define handleAddTodo function
steps.instruction: Inside the TodoList component, define a function named handleAddTodo. This function should create a new todo object from the inputText state and add it to the todos array using setTodos.
steps.hint: Create a function that takes no parameters. Inside it, use setTodos to update the state by spreading the existing todos array and adding a new todo object at the end.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleAddTodo function is defined inside the component that creates a new todo object and updates the todos state.
successCriteria: The code should include a function named handleAddTodo that creates a new todo object with id, text, and completed properties, and calls setTodos to add it to the existing todos array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the handleAddTodo function that will add new todos to your list.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function creates a complete todo object with all required properties (id, text, completed) and properly updates the todos state using setTodos.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleAddTodo function isn't defined correctly. Remember to create a function that builds a new todo object and updates the todos state using setTodos.

steps.title: Define handleToggleTodo function
steps.instruction: Define a function named handleToggleTodo that toggles the completed property of a todo by its id. The function should take a todo id as a parameter and update the todos state accordingly.
steps.hint: Create a function that receives an id parameter. Inside, use setTodos with the previous state to map over todos and toggle the completed property for the matching todo.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleToggleTodo function is defined that toggles the completed status of a todo by its id.
successCriteria: Function named handleToggleTodo is defined
Function takes an id parameter of type number
Function uses setTodos to update state
Function maps over previous todos and toggles completed for matching id
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the handleToggleTodo function. This function will allow users to mark todos as completed or incomplete by clicking on them.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but there are some issues. Make sure your function: 1) is named handleToggleTodo, 2) takes an id parameter, 3) uses setTodos to update state, and 4) properly toggles the completed property for the matching todo.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleToggleTodo function is not defined correctly. Review the example and try again. Remember to create a function that toggles the completed status of a todo by its id.

steps.title: Define handleDeleteTodo function
steps.instruction: Define a function named handleDeleteTodo that takes a todo id as a parameter and removes that todo from the todos array by its id.
steps.hint: Use the setTodos function to update the state by filtering out the todo with the matching id.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleDeleteTodo function that filters the todos array to remove a todo by its id.
successCriteria: Function named handleDeleteTodo
Takes an id parameter (type number)
Uses setTodos to update state
Filters todos array to remove matching id
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a delete handler that removes todos by their id.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function takes an id parameter and uses setTodos with a filter to remove the matching todo.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleDeleteTodo function isn't quite right. It should take an id parameter and use setTodos to filter out the todo with that id.

steps.title: Return the main container div
steps.instruction: In your TodoList component, return a div element that will contain the todo list interface. This div should wrap around the existing h1 element.
steps.hint: Make sure the div is the top-level JSX element returned from the component.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component returns a div element containing the h1 element.
successCriteria: The component returns JSX
The top-level element is a div
The div contains the existing h1 element
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've set up the main container div for your todo list interface.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're returning a div element that wraps around the h1 element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component should return a div element containing the h1 element. Check your JSX structure.

steps.title: Add input field and add button
steps.instruction: Inside the return statement of your TodoList component, add an input field and a button after the h1 element. The input should have its value bound to the inputText state and update that state on change. The button should call handleAddTodo when clicked.
steps.hint: Use an input element with value={inputText} and onChange={(e) => setInputText(e.target.value)}. Add a button with onClick={handleAddTodo}.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will display an input field and an 'Add' button below the heading. The input will reflect the current inputText state, and typing in it will update that state. Clicking the button will trigger the handleAddTodo function (though it won't do anything yet).
successCriteria: The code should include an input element with value={inputText} and onChange={(e) => setInputText(e.target.value)} attributes, and a button element with onClick={handleAddTodo} attribute, both placed inside the div after the h1.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the input field and button. The input is now bound to the inputText state, and the button is ready to call handleAddTodo when clicked.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some elements, but make sure you have both an input with value and onChange attributes bound to inputText, and a button with onClick calling handleAddTodo.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input field and button are not correctly added. Ensure you have an input element with value={inputText} and onChange={(e) => setInputText(e.target.value)}, and a button with onClick={handleAddTodo}.

steps.title: Map and display todos list
steps.instruction: Inside the return statement of your TodoList component, map through the todos array and render each todo's text and completed status.
steps.hint: Use the map method on the todos array to create an array of JSX elements. For each todo, display its text and completed status.
steps.expectedOutcome: The todos array will be rendered as a list of elements showing each todo's text and completed status.
successCriteria: The code must include a map method call on the todos array inside the return statement, generating JSX elements that display each todo's text and completed status.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully mapped through the todos array and rendered each todo's details. This displays the list of todos in your UI.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're mapping through the todos array and displaying both the text and completed status for each todo.
steps.feedbackWrong: The todos list isn't being displayed correctly. Remember to use the map method on the todos array inside your return statement to create JSX elements for each todo.

steps.title: Add toggle and delete buttons for each todo
steps.instruction: Inside the existing map function for todos, add a toggle button with onClick that calls handleToggleTodo(todo.id) and a delete button with onClick that calls handleDeleteTodo(todo.id) for each todo item.
steps.hint: Add two <button> elements inside each todo item's JSX. The toggle button should have text like 'Toggle' and onClick={() => handleToggleTodo(todo.id)}. The delete button should have text like 'Delete' and onClick={() => handleDeleteTodo(todo.id)}.
steps.expectedOutcome: Each todo item in the list will have two buttons: one to toggle its completion status and one to delete it.
successCriteria: Add a toggle button inside the map function
Toggle button has onClick calling handleToggleTodo with todo.id
Add a delete button inside the map function
Delete button has onClick calling handleDeleteTodo with todo.id
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added interactive toggle and delete buttons to each todo item. The todo list is now fully functional.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some buttons, but make sure you have both a toggle button and a delete button for each todo, and that they correctly call the corresponding handler functions with todo.id.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggle and delete buttons are missing or incorrectly implemented. Check that you added both buttons inside the map function and that their onClick handlers call handleToggleTodo(todo.id) and handleDeleteTodo(todo.id).
